newsitem.title: USA: Fed expected to add reserves via term system RPs.
newsitem.headline: Fed expected to add reserves via term system RPs.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is likely to add temporary reserves to the banking system on Monday through term system repurchase agreements as it responds to seasonal reserve needs and to shifts related to the April 15 income tax date, economists said.

Federal funds were trading at 5-1/2 percent, the Fed's target for the rate, in mid-morning dealings but some upward pressure on the rate could occur heading into the April 15 personal income tax date on Tuesday, they said.
James Glassman, senior economist at Chase Securities Inc, said he expects the Fed to conduct term system repurchase agreements, "possibly a 10-day RP, replacing the 14-day RP that is rolling off."
Glassman estimated the Fed's add need at $5.0 billion and said he would not be surprised by a three-day system repurchase operation.
"Conceivably, they could do three-day RPs and wait for the second week (of the two-week bank reserve maintenance period) to step it up a little," he said.
Tax payments tend to raise the U.S. Treasury's balance at the Fed which drains reserves from the banking system.
